edition.locus: Gebhardt II.15-20 (the gods never lived; the timeless God; the devil's envy)

source_text: Εἰ δὲ μαθεῖν ὅτι ἀληθές ἐστιν τοῦτο· ἄρον τὴν τιμήν σου ἀπ᾽ αὐτῶν ἣν δοκεῖς προσφέρειν αὐτοῖς, καὶ γνώσῃ ὅτι οὐθέν εἰσιν, ὕλη γῆς ὑπάρχοντα καὶ τῷ χρόνῳ φθειρόμενα. Ὁ γὰρ θεὸς ἡμῶν ἄχρονος ὢν καὶ τοὺς αἰῶνας ποιήσας, αὐτὸς ἄφθαρτος καὶ αἰώνιος διαμένει, ὁ αὐτὸς ἀεὶ ὤν, μήτε αὔξησιν μήτε μείωσιν ἐπιδεχόμενος, οὗτοι δὲ καὶ γίνονται ὑπὸ ἀνθρώπων καὶ φθείρονται, ὡς ἔφην, ὑπὸ τοῦ χρόνου. Τὸ δὲ χρησμεύειν καὶ ἀπατᾶν αὐτοὺς μὴ θαυμάσῃς· ὁ γὰρ διάβολος ἀπ᾽ ἀρχῆς πεσὼν ἐκ τῆς ἐνδόξου αὐτοῦ τάξεως οἰκείᾳ μοχθηρίᾳ τὴν πρὸς τὸν ἄνθρωπον τοῦ θεοῦ στοργὴν καταργεῖ καὶ καταπιεζόμενος ὑπὸ τῶν ἁγίων τούτοις ἀνταγωνίζεται καὶ προκατασκευάζει πολέμους καὶ προλαμβάνων ἀπαγγέλλει τοῖς ἰδίοις. Ὁμοίως καὶ ἐκ τῶν καθ᾽ ἡμέραν ἡμῖν συμβαινόντων, ἀρχαιότερος ὢν τοῦ χρόνου, ἀποπειράσας τὰ συμβησόμενα προλέγει, ἅπερ αὐτὸς μέλλει κακοποιεῖν. Ἔσχεν γὰρ ἐκ τῆς ἀποφάσεως τοῦ θεοῦ τὴν ἀδικίαν καὶ τὸ εἰδέναι, καὶ κατὰ συγχώρησιν θεοῦ πειράζει τὸν ἄνθρωπον, ζητῶν πλανῆσαι τῆς εὐσεβείας. Πείσθητε οὖν μοι, ὑπατικέ, ὅτι ἐν ματαιότητί ἐστε οὐ μικρᾷ.
pass_a_gloss: If you want to learn that this is true: take away your honor from them which you think you offer to them, and you will know that they are nothing, being matter of earth and being corrupted by time. For our God, being timeless and having made the ages, himself remains imperishable and eternal, always being the same, admitting neither increase nor decrease, but these both come into being by men and are corrupted, as I said, by time. Do not wonder at their giving oracles and deceiving; for the devil, having fallen from the beginning from his glorious rank by his own wickedness, annuls God's love toward man and, being pressed hard by the holy ones, contends against them and prepares wars beforehand and, forestalling, announces to his own. Likewise also from the things happening daily to us, being older than time, having tested what is going to happen he foretells, things which he himself is about to do for harm. For he received from God's judgment both wrongdoing and knowing, and by God's permission he tempts man, seeking to lead astray from piety. Be persuaded by me, consular, that you are in no small vanity.
pass_b_english: If you would learn that this is true, strip your reverence away from them, the reverence you imagine you render them, and you will see that they are nothing, mere earthly stuff wasting away with time. For our God is beyond time and made the ages themselves, and he abides imperishable and everlasting, ever the same, accepting neither growth nor lessening, while these gods both are fashioned by human hands and rot, as I have said, under time.

Do not marvel that they utter oracles and cheat men, for the devil, fallen from the beginning out of his glorious station through his own depravity, labors to undo God's love for man, and when the saints press him hard he fights back against them, staging wars in advance and telling his own beforehand what is coming. In the same way, from what befalls us day by day, since he is older than this present order, he tests what is likely to happen and predicts it, the very evils he himself means to inflict. For from God's sentence he has both his wrongdoing and his knowing, and he tempts man only by God's leave, seeking to seduce him from true worship. Trust me then, O consular, that you stand in no small futility.

lemmas.gloss: being corrupted or decaying over time

choices.term: ἄρον τὴν τιμήν σου ἀπ᾽ αὐτῶν
choices.english: strip your reverence away from them
choices.why: aorist imperative of αἴρω with ἀπό denotes removal, and τιμή here is cultic honor, not price or value
neuter singular used adverbially for persons to stress lack of being rather than masculine οὐδένες
vocative singular address to a former consul, retaining Roman title rather than generalizing to friend
κατά with accusative marks governing condition, so tempting is limited permission, not commission
